unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts two things the first draft kept: the sentence saying Poincare alone felt the historian's need of unity, and the paragraph explaining that Poincare assumes the alternation of simple and complex that Adams had to surrender. The result is a one-line paragraph, 'green with horror', with no stated cause.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Both contradictory Poincare quotations stay together, as the plan requires, and 'but suddenly he fell on another view' still marks the turn.

evidence.quote: but he seemed to be the only authority in science who felt what a historian felt so strongly--the need of unity in a universe.
assuming that the past showed alternating phases of simple and complex--the precise point that Adams, after fifty years of effort, found himself forced to surrender
He burned to ask whether M. Poincare knew any history
Here at last was a fixed point. History and mathematics agreed. "Considering everything we have made some approach towards unity."
A mathematical paradise of endless displacement promised eternal bliss to the mathematician, but turned the historian green with horror.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'M. Poincare seemed to be the only authority in science who felt ... the need of unity in a universe.' Append to paragraph 11 a clause such as 'since he assumed alternating phases of simple and complex--the precise point that Adams, after fifty years of effort, found himself forced to surrender.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (Poincare's irony and the alternation that turns the historian green)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: 'History and mathematics agreed' no longer says what they agreed on. The horror reads as a generic reaction rather than as the irony that the mathematician's paradise is the kinetic gas the 'weary Titan of Unity' fears.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Poincare sequence loses its 'need of unity' frame and the reason for the historian's horror

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts two sentences the first draft kept. One is 'She did not think of her universe as a raft to which the limpets stuck', which explicitly opposes her ordered universe to science's 'sensual raft' in the earlier paragraph about Pearson's axe. The other is 'Man knew it was true because he made it'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'which she knew to be unity because she had made it' preserves part of the self-made-universe idea.

evidence.quote: She did not think of her universe as a raft to which the limpets stuck for life in the surge of a supersensual chaos
Man knew it was true because he made it, and he loved it for the same reason.
She did not think of her universe as a raft to which the limpets stuck
leaving science adrift on a sensual raft in the midst of a supersensual chaos
She conceived herself and her family as the centre and flower of an ordered universe

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the raft/limpet clause before 'she conceived herself' and the 'Man knew it was true' sentence after the nacre sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (pearl-oyster image and woman's ordered universe)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The oyster section loses its tie to the raft on which Adams finds himself. It also loses its echo of Pearson's 'Order was the dream of man', so the closing image reads more as a detached digression.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Woman's universe no longer contrasted with the raft; man-made truth line cut

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision drops two things the first draft kept. One is the statement that history needs only the admission of ignorance. The other is the gloss on Zeno's arrow, 'continuous from the beginning of time, and discontinuous at each successive point'. Without the gloss, 'familiar and inexplicable since Zeno' is opaque.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The phrase 'mere instrument of measure' and the 'we are probably incapable of discovering' dictum still convey the stance of ignorance.

evidence.quote: all it needed to know was the admission of ignorance; the mere fact of multiplicity baffling science.
familiar and inexplicable since Zeno and his arrow: continuous from the beginning of time, and discontinuous at each successive point.
History needed only the admission of ignorance; the mere fact of multiplicity baffling science.
radium was merely the next position, familiar and inexplicable since Zeno and his arrow.
Only in 1900, the continuity snapped.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's 'History needed only the admission of ignorance; the mere fact of multiplicity baffling science.' Also restore the colon clause after 'Zeno and his arrow'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (historian as instrument; radium as next point since Zeno)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The catalogue of ignorance no longer resolves into Adams's method, which the plan treats as a recurring mechanism. The continuity/discontinuity idea that the cannon-ball paragraph turns on is no longer prepared.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Admission of ignorance and the Zeno continuity gloss cut before 'the continuity snapped'

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts two grounds the first draft kept for 'in no way responsible': that Adams had submitted to force all his life, and that he never invented his facts because authorities furnished them.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'according to Helmholz, Ernst Mach, and Arthur Balfour' implicitly attributes the view to others.

evidence.quote: He never invented his facts; they were furnished him by the only authorities he could find.
but he had submitted to force all his life, and he meant to accept it for the future as for the past.
He never invented his facts; they were furnished him by the only authorities he could find.
For this theory, Adams felt himself in no way responsible. As for himself, according to Helmholz, Ernst Mach, and Arthur Balfour

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinsert 'He never invented his facts; they were furnished him by the only authorities he could find.' after the disclaimer.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: planning omission (the essential list does not name this support, but its loss leaves a residue)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The disclaimer becomes an unexplained assertion. It loses the link to the plan's mechanism of submission to force and to the paragraph's self-deprecating logic.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Adams's disclaimer of responsibility left without its grounds

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft had already cut Hegel's 'every notion included its own negation', which leaves 'the negation' unexplained. The revision also cuts 'For himself he knew ... he would be forced to enter supersensual chaos'. 'Every one had done it' now attaches to 'thinking about it' or to 'know the unknowable' rather than to entering supersensual chaos.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The closing 'sailed gaily into the supersensual' partly clarifies what 'it' means.

evidence.quote: For himself he knew, that, in spite of all the Englishmen that ever lived, he would be forced to enter supersensual chaos
Even Hegel, who taught that every notion included its own negation, used the negation only to reach a "larger synthesis,"
Even Hegel used the negation only to reach a "larger synthesis," till he reached the universal which thinks itself
every one went on thinking about it. From Pythagoras to Herbert Spencer, every one had done it
Even Hegel used the negation only to reach a "larger synthesis."

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'For himself he knew ... forced to enter supersensual chaos' sentence. Add 'who taught that every notion included its own negation,' after 'Hegel'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: required (everyone from Pythagoras to Hegel sailed into the supersensual)
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The argument that all thinkers sailed into the supersensual is blurred. Adams's personal compulsion to enter chaos also disappears from the paragraph.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Paragraph 4 leaves 'done it' and 'the negation' without antecedents

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts Adams's wonder that a mind as superior as Gibbs's could find help anywhere, and the confession 'He never found out what it could have taught' Gibbs. It also flattens 'half-a-dozen empires interested ... less than the rise of the Grammar' into a neutral statement of preparation.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The phrase 'try to find out what Karl Pearson could have taught Willard Gibbs' survives and implies the puzzle.

evidence.quote: and the idea that a man so incomparably superior should find help anywhere filled him with wonder.
the fall or rise of half-a-dozen empires interested a student of history less than the rise of the "Grammar of Science,"
He never found out what it could have taught a master like Willard Gibbs.
Under the silent influence of Langley, a student of history was prepared to expect the rise of the "Grammar of Science."

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'He never found out what it could have taught a master like Willard Gibbs.' Also restore the first draft's empires sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The quest's irony, a confessed failure to learn what Pearson taught Gibbs, and the historian's comic sense of scale are lost from the chapter's first beat.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Opening loses its Gibbs wonder, the confession of failure, and the empires comparison
